title: Bread and Butter Pudding
subtitle: Layered bread pudding baked in custard
excerpt: Thick slices of buttered white bread soaked in vanilla custard, baked until the top is golden and crisp and the inside is creamy and set. The definitive use of stale bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bread and butter pudding appears in British cookbooks from the 18th century as a thrifty way to use stale bread. The principle is simple: buttered bread baked in a sweetened egg and milk custard. For much of its history it was considered plain nursery food. Its rehabilitation into a restaurant dessert began in the 1980s with versions using enriched brioche or croissants in place of plain white bread. The classic version with white bread and sultanas remains the most satisfying: the crusts catch and caramelise against the hot sides of the dish while the centre stays luscious and just set. A minimum of 30 minutes soaking before baking is essential for the bread to absorb the custard properly.

recipeTools.notes: A 25 cm oven-proof ceramic or glass dish.

content.text: Use bread that is a day old: stale bread absorbs the custard much more efficiently than fresh. Butter the bread thickly, right to the edges. Let the assembled pudding soak for at least 30 minutes, pressing the bread gently down into the custard several times. The pudding is ready when the custard is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. It will continue to firm up as it rests.

items.preparation: softened, plus extra for the dish

content.text: Butter each slice of bread generously. Cut in half diagonally. Butter an oven-proof dish. Layer the bread slices, butter-side up and overlapping slightly, scattering the sultanas between layers.
Whisk together the milk, cream, eggs, egg yolks, caster sugar, and vanilla. Pour slowly and evenly over the bread. Press the bread gently down. Leave to soak for at least 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Grate nutmeg over the top and scatter with demerara sugar. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the custard is just set and the top is golden and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
